title: The test-bed produced runs nobody should have believed
description:
One session produced six measurements that were wrong in six different ways, and
every one looked like an ordinary result. This bead is the work that makes that
harder, and the record of what each rule is for.

## What went wrong, and how it looked

- two runners at once. Two scripts waiting on the same 'is a run going' check
  both started, three times. Each map change pulled the other's mission out from
  under it, and both wrote files.
- a stale plugin. A run with --no-build measured a mod loaded two hours earlier
  and reported the fix doing nothing. The version was never checked.
- the mission named on a map already up. mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 reported
  itself as the current popfile and built none of its robots, nine times across
  four builds, and every one was recorded as a loss.
- the mission named before the map. A changelevel resets tf_mvm_popfile, so the
  name was thrown away and the run played the map's own mission.
- a wave nobody fought. Twenty two robots and an empty RED still writes a file,
  and every number in it is zero.
- a grep read wrong. A multi-file grep -c gave a column of per-file counts and I
  read it as a total, twice, and reported a recovery that had fired 114 times as
  never firing.

The shape they share: the test-bed could not tell a run that measured nothing
from a run that measured a mission nobody wins. Both are a file of zeros.

## What is being done

A Go runner, testbed/cmd/testbed, that refuses rather than produces. Every rule
in it is one of the above.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Done so far, all pushed.

testbed/cmd/testbed replaces run.sh, ab.sh, sweep.sh and batch.sh. The three
wrappers each carried their own idea of what a valid run was, which is how one
mistake kept reappearing in different clothes. One place decides now.

Refusals, each one of the failures above:

- a lock file holds the test-bed, and a second runner is told who has it
- the version in source/tf2_defenderbots.sp is compared with the version the
  server reports, and a mismatch stops the run
- the map is loaded, then the mission named, then the mission verified
- RED must hold the lineup before a wave counts

Watching, rather than waiting and reading the wreckage:

- no robot on BLU for five polls: the mission is loaded and not playing
- the statistics file not growing for six polls: the plugin is gone
- RED emptying mid-wave: the rest measures a team nobody asked for
- rcon stops answering: a crash in what is being measured, counted as one

Each names its reason in about a minute instead of a twenty five minute timeout
and an empty file.

Reporting carries the band rule from docs/testbed-metrics.md: it says outright
when an arm's median falls inside the control's quartiles, when the control is
too small for a band, and when a column was never written to. That last one came
from a test catching the report giving a confident verdict about two columns of
zeros.

Tests cover the lock refusing a second runner, arm parsing, all three verdicts,
and all four watcher rules.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Still to do, in the order they matter:

- the smoke test has not passed yet. The runner refuses on Decoy with 'RED never
  reached 6 defenders', which is the point of it, but the cause is not fully
  chased: compose now gets the run's shape and the arm is set after the map
  load, and it still has to be seen filling RED end to end.
- crash detection is rcon going quiet. run.sh also grepped the container log for
  'core dumped', which catches a crash the container restarts out of before a
  poll notices. Worth carrying over.
- run-native.sh is still shell and still calls the removed flags. Either it is
  ported or it is deleted.
- nothing checks the map is one the server actually has. A typo gives a
  changelevel that quietly does nothing, and the run then measures whatever was
  already loaded. The mission is verified and the map is not.
- results are written per attempt with no record of what produced them. A file
  should carry its arm, its build version and its preconditions, so a stale
  file cannot be read as a fresh one.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The smoke test found a fault in the runner itself, which is the point of it.

A changelevel onto the map the server was already on left RED at nought
defenders, every time, on Decoy: a map that fills fine from a fresh container.
The mod disables its bots in OnMapStart and waits to be started again, so the
extra map load undid the thing the run needs.

The container recreate is already a map load, and it is the one the mission gets
named after, which is the order Mannhunt needs. So the changelevel now only
happens when the server is on a different map.

Three attempts at this, and the shape is worth keeping: each fix was right about
the thing it fixed and wrong about being the last one. exec server.cfg was
missing, then the run's shape never reached compose, then the arm was set before
the map load wiped it, then the lineup was awaited before the nudge that causes
it, then the map load itself was the fault. The old shell had none of these
checks and would have produced a file for every one of them.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The runner passes its preconditions. Decoy, mvm_decoy_advanced:

  the server is running 2.27.0, which is what the source says
  already on mvm_decoy
  naming mission mvm_decoy_advanced
  waiting for the mod to start filling RED
  RED holds 6 defenders

Version checked, map not needlessly reloaded, mission named after the load,
lineup verified. The wave is playing and the watcher has it.

That is the fifth fix and the first pass. Worth noting what the sequence cost:
five wrong answers, each of which the old shell would have turned into a results
file rather than a refusal. The runner found every one within a minute of
starting, which is the whole argument for it.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The runner produced its first real result, and produced two more faults on the
way, both in itself.

  smoke on mvm_decoy, mvm_decoy_advanced
  1 attempt, 5 waves, 0 cleared, 0 crashes, 0 empty

Faults found by running it:

- the roster was read from player names. Decoy's robots are named Pyro,
  Heavyweight and Giant, and only some missions name them TFBot, so fourteen
  robots on BLU counted as defenders: the precondition passed on robots alone
  and then called the wave stalled because BLU read empty. The host plugin now
  answers mvmbots_roster from the game.
- the wait loop had no success exit. A run with its wave after two minutes
  polled on to the sixteen minute timeout and collected four more, all of them
  wave one lost and retried.
- the single-arm report added waves to empties and called it attempts, so one
  attempt reading five waves printed as five attempts.

The pattern in the first is the same one that cost the recovery diagnosis
earlier: a fact inferred from a proxy that usually correlates with it. Names
correlate with team on Mannworks and not on Decoy.

title: Bots replaced mid-wave never shop at the break they come back in
description:
Reported: 'i tried replacing all my bots after wave 1 start, and they just did
not buy anything! as if they did not have any money'.

## What is certain

A team change during a running wave is held: Command_ReseatBots sets
m_bRecyclePending, says the new team takes effect when the wave ends, and
Reseat_OnBreak does the kicking.

Reseat_OnBreak is called from Event_MvmWaveComplete and Event_MvmWaveFailed, in
both cases at the top, above the comment that reads 'Before anything below sends
the engineers off to shop'. So the old bots are kicked at the moment the break
opens, and the replacements join after it.

## What is not certain

Whether that ordering is the fault. A bot that joins through the normal path
gets SetCurrencyWithBundles(GetStartingCurrency + GetAcquiredCreditsOfAllWaves)
in events.sp, so it should hold the money the wave earned. 'As if they did not
have any money' is a symptom, and a bot that has money but was never sent to
shop looks the same from a seat.

Two candidates, and they are not exclusive:

- the break's shopping pass has already gone by the time the new bots are in,
  so they hold their credits and never spend them
- the credits are genuinely wrong, and the join path grants less than the wave
  earned

## How to tell them apart

The log answers it without a guess. Each break prints one 'Shopping: <name>
stopped, ... N credits left' per bot, and the recycle prints 'Reseat: recycled N
bot(s) held from mid-wave'. Replace the team mid-wave, then read the break that
follows:

- no Shopping line at all for the new names: the ordering is the fault
- a Shopping line saying 0 credits left with nothing bought: the credits are

This is worth a testbed run rather than a play-test, since the reseat and the
break are both scriptable.
close_reason:
Not a bug. The reporter had the purchase-in-chat setting off, so the buys
happened and nothing printed them.

Worth keeping the shape of this one: the whole bead was built on an absence.
'They did not buy anything' was read off missing chat lines, and the setting
that writes those lines is off by default. An absent log line says nothing about
whether the thing happened.

One loose end from reading the code, recorded here rather than left as an open
P0 nobody has seen: Reseat_OnBreak runs at the top of Event_MvmWaveComplete,
above the comment that says 'Before anything below sends the engineers off to
shop'. Whether a bot that rejoins there still catches that break's shopping pass
is untested. No symptom has ever pointed at it, so it stays a note.

title: The engineer walks the map to place his teleporter exit
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27, Cowser on Bigrock.

  "the engineer at start of wave places all of it at front, then goes
   AAAAAAAALLLLL the way back to place the exit"
  "instead of where it's more helpful at the front"

And on the spot itself: "wtf is this exit spot", then after a fix, "ok this one
is sliiiiiightly better BUT IT'S STILL IN MAIN BOT PATH".

omaewh4 confirmed the cause is likely ours: "maybe the manual spot i saved is
broken, will need to redo this", and "Bigrock might need some more work".

## Two faults, and they are separate

The walk. An engineer that builds his nest at the front and then crosses the
map to place an exit spends the opening of the wave out of position, undefended,
and away from the sentry he just built. Whatever picks the exit spot is not
considering how far it is from the rest of his buildings.

The spot. Bigrock's registered exit spot sits in the main bot path. A teleporter
exit there is walked into, blocks the lane it is meant to feed, and is the first
thing a robot hits.

## Why P0

Same reason as the freeze: half of what this mod does is engineer behaviour, and
this one takes the engineer off the field at the exact moment the wave starts.

## Where to look

configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_bigrock.cfg holds the spots. mvm-1pq already fixed
one exit built inside the sentry's blast radius, so the pattern of a spot chosen
without regard to what is around it has bitten before.

The walk is behaviour rather than config: the exit spot wants choosing near the
nest, or the exit wants building before the engineer commits to the front.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Correcting what I wrote above. I had the fix backwards.

The exit spot on the rock is the right spot. The engineer cannot jump onto it,
so he falls back to somewhere he can walk to, and that somewhere is the main bot
path. Moving the spot would be fixing the symptom and losing a good position.

  "the spot is on a rock where the engineer cant jump, make the engineer be able
   to jump instead of putting the teleporter on the path (the teleporter should
   be up there on the rocks)"

So the bug is the engineer's, not the map config's:

- he cannot reach a spot that needs a jump
- and what he does instead is build in the lane everything walks down

Both halves want fixing, and the second is the dangerous one. A fallback that
picks a spot in the bot path is worse than no fallback, because it puts a
building where it blocks the lane it is meant to feed and is the first thing a
robot hits. mvm-1pq fixed an exit built inside the sentry's blast for the same
reason: a fallback that does not look at what is around it.

The walk in the original description still stands as its own fault: building the
nest at the front and then crossing the map for the exit leaves him out of
position at the wave start.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed the reach, not the spot, in source/redbots3/behavior/engineerbuildteleporter.sp.

What was happening on Bigrock. The exit spot is "-178 3921 318"; the two nests
are at z 250 and 260, so the spot sits about seventy units up on the rock.
BuildStandPoint takes the ring point beside the spot and snaps it to the nearest
nav area within 120 units, and the nav there is the floor below, which is inside
BUILD_STAND_STOREY (100) so it is accepted. He walks to the foot of the rock,
aims up at a spot over his head, IsPlacementOK refuses every one of the eight
sides, and the exit branch then sets the reach deadline to now, which makes
outOfTime true, which sets stand = GetAbsOrigin(actor). That is the man standing
at the bottom of the rock in the lane. "IT'S STILL IN MAIN BOT PATH" is that
line.

Two changes.

1. He climbs. TeleporterClimbToSpot: when the spot is between 24 and 72 units
above his feet and within 140 units horizontally, he looks at it and presses
IN_FORWARD | IN_JUMP | IN_DUCK for 0.3s, once every 0.7s, at most six times.
24 is above a step, 72 is a crouch jump, so anything higher is a wall and he
does not try. Nothing in this mod had ever pressed IN_JUMP at a piece of ground
before; the Scout combat jump is the only other IN_JUMP in the tree.
When he makes it, the stand point is set to where he landed rather than
recomputed, because recomputing asks the nav mesh and the nav mesh answers with
the floor he just left, which is the walk back down.

2. The fallback stops settling for where he stands. A named exit spot that
beats him now falls back once to the nest ring (TeleporterFallBackToNest), which
is the same ring every map that names no exit already uses: beside his own
sentry, outside BUSTER_BLAST_RANGE, and a spot rather than an accident. Only if
that ring also refuses him does the old build-at-my-feet apply. This is the
"settling for where you stand" line in how-bots-break.md, and it is the half
that put the building in the lane.

The file's own comment claimed "He is standing at his nest when this runs out",
which is only true when the map names no exit spot. Corrected.

Compiles clean against the testbed's spcomp. Not verified in play: I was told
not to run anything, a measurement is in flight.

What would prove it. A Bigrock run, and the number is printSpotUse: the median
distance from the sampled teleporter exit to "-178 3921 318" per wave. Today
that should be a few hundred units (he builds at the bottom of the rock); the
fix should put it near zero, or, if the crouch jump does not carry him, put it
at the nest instead of in the lane, which is still the better half. Both
outcomes are readable from the same line, which is why it is worth measuring
even if the jump turns out not to work.

Not done, and why:

- No feature switch. The A/B wants a FEATURE_ENGINEER_CLIMBS entry, and that is
  a line in source/redbots3/features.sp, which I was told not to touch. Whoever
  owns that file needs the enum member and the MakeFeature call; the two call
  sites in engineerbuildteleporter.sp are the climb block in Update and
  TeleporterFallBackToNest.
- The walk from the original description. NearestFreeExitSpot already picks the
  named exit nearest the nest, and on Bigrock that is 400-700 units from either
  nest, not a map crossing. The long walk in the report is the entrance, which
  is at the spawn by definition. Untouched.
- mvm-fgs stays open: it needs a Bigrock run to verify and I could not run one.
- The Rottenburg P1 (exit near a fall players die on) is untouched. Nothing here
  looks at what is under or beside an exit spot; that wants its own check.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fix merged into main behind FEATURE_ENGINEER_CLIMBS, off by default.

The cause, found by reading rather than guessing: Bigrock's exit spot is at
-178 3921 318 and both nests sit at z 250 to 260, so the spot is about 70 units
up the rock. BuildStandPoint snaps the ring point to the nearest nav area within
120 units and gets the floor below, 68 down, which is inside BUILD_STAND_STOREY
of 100 and so passes. He walks to the foot of the rock, IsPlacementOK refuses all

own position. That one line is the exit in the bot lane.

Two changes:

- he crouch jumps. A named spot 24 to 72 units above his feet and within 140

  at 6 attempts and still inside the 12s reach clock. 24 clears a step, 72 is a
  crouch jump, so a wall is never attempted. On landing the stand point is where
  he landed: recomputing it asks the nav mesh and gets the floor he just left.
- the fallback stops settling for where he stands. A named exit spot that beats
  him now falls back to the nest ring first, the same ring every map naming no

The switch is the A/B, three call sites gated, default off like the path cap.
Compiles clean.

The run: Bigrock, read through printSpotUse, median distance from the sampled
exit to -178 3921 318 per wave. A few hundred units today. Near zero says the
jump carries; at the nest instead of the lane is still the better half. Both
read off the same line.

Not this bead: the long walk in the original report is the entrance, which is at

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Bigrock A/B measured, four attempts each arm, mvm_bigrock_advanced1 wave 1.

Distance from the sampled teleporter exit to the rock spot -178 3921 318:

  climb=off   72 samples   median 3384   min 3351   none under 100
  climb=on   116 samples   median  237   min  237   none under 100

So the fallback half works and the jump half does not.

Off, the exit is 3384 units away: that is the build-at-my-feet branch putting it
wherever the walk gave up, which is the reported bug. On, it is 237 units away
and never varies, which is the nest ring. The change moved the exit off the lane
and next to the sentry, which was the second of the two things it was meant to
do.

It never once reached the spot. Not a single sample under 100 units, and the
minimum equals the median, so the engineer is not landing on the rock at all,
he is going straight to the ring. Either the 24 to 72 unit window does not match
the real height from where he stands, or the crouch jump does not carry him, or
TeleporterClimbToSpot is not being reached before the fallback fires. The three
are separable by logging the height difference it computes.

Wave outcome says nothing here: all sixteen waves lost in both arms, and the
medians of robot kills overlap. Bigrock advanced1 wave 1 is not a wave this team
clears, so it cannot rank the arms. The distance is the measure.

One crash, in climb=on attempt 1, which produced no wave at all. Three of the
other seven attempts on that arm ran clean, so it does not look like the climb
causing it, but one crash in eight is not a number that clears anything either.
Bigrock is a map with engineers, and [[mvm-ipf]] is about engineers crashing.

Keeping FEATURE_ENGINEER_CLIMBS off. Half a fix behind a switch that is off is
not shipped, and the jump is the half that was asked for.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Status. Half fixed and the half that shipped is the half that was not asked for.

Measured on Bigrock, four attempts each arm: the exit moved from 3384 units off
the rock spot to 237, which is the nest ring. The fallback works. The crouch
jump does not: not one sample under 100 units, and the minimum equals the median,
so he never lands on the rock at all.

FEATURE_ENGINEER_CLIMBS stays off. Half a fix behind a switch that is off is not
shipped.

What it needs next is instrumentation rather than another attempt: log the height
difference TeleporterClimbToSpot computes and whether it is reached before the
fallback fires. Three candidates and they are separable: the 24 to 72 unit window
does not match the real height, the jump does not carry, or the branch is never
reached.

title: The engineer freezes and never builds anything
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27.

Philiard: "the Engineer bot seems a bit broken. At least on Mean Machines on
Mannworks, he gets permanently stuck in this one spot and never actually places
any of his buildings."

Permanently, and no buildings at all. A team without a sentry on an Advanced
mission is a team that loses, so this is not a bot playing badly: it is a seat
doing nothing for the whole run.

## Why P0

Half of what this mod does is engineer behaviour. An engineer that never builds
takes the nest, the dispenser and the teleporters out of the team at once.

## What is already known

Three beads describe the same shape on other maps, and this is the fourth
report:

- mvm-6rt, freezes during setup on Decoy
- mvm-ipf, stuck inside a prop on Mannhunt
- mvm-zx0, leaves the nest mid-wave hunting metal and gets stuck on geometry

And the test-bed has caught it in the log without anybody reporting it:

  stuck: Waldo (engineer) at 346 551 544 for 12s,
         MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderEngineerIdle < ScenarioMonitor

Twelve seconds later the engine watchdog killed the server, inside
NavAreaBuildPath. So a stuck engineer is not only a lost seat, it is a suspect
in the crash on mvm-cf3.

## Where to start

The stuck line names the action stack, so the test-bed can already say which
behaviour is holding it. Mannworks with Mean Machines is a reproduction nobody
had before: run it, read the stack, and find what the engineer is waiting for
that never comes.

kelly-cs's spawn recovery in v2.20.0 moves a bot that cannot leave spawn. This
is a bot that has left spawn and then stops, so that recovery does not cover it.
close_reason: Fixed and measured on the reproduction. A wedged bot is moved to the nearest walkable nav area after three stucks at one spot, in the watchdog where a behaviour reset cannot undo it. Mannworks with Mean Machines went from crashing at 0 waves with no sentries built to 4 of 4 waves, no crash, and 42 sentries. The remaining cause, whatever keeps walking him into that spot, is filed separately.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Reproduced, root-caused, and my first two attempts at the fix were both wrong in
the same way.

## The reproduction

Mannworks with Mean Machines, on the test-bed:

  stuck: Wesley (engineer) at 1014 885 274 for 12s,
         MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderBuildSentrygun < DefenderEngineerIdle

Nineteen times, the same coordinates, inside the sentry build action, and never
a sentry. That is Philiard's report exactly.

## The cause: two timers chasing each other

STUCK_TIME is 12.0 and SENTRY_REACH_TIME is 12.0.

The stuck watchdog fires at twelve seconds and calls ResetIntentionInterface,
which resets the whole behaviour tree. That restarts the build action, whose
OnStart re-arms the reach deadline to now plus twelve. So the deadline that
would have made him give the spot up is pushed forward every time he is rescued,
and he is rescued into the same trap for the rest of the mission.

## Two wrong fixes, both defeated by the same reset

First I added the missing branch: the give-up path only ran when he was already
near the spot, so an engineer who never arrives never reached it. Real gap, and
useless here, because it hangs off the same deadline. The verification run
proved it: the bug happened and the new log line never appeared.

Then I counted stucks per attempt, and marked the count in OnStart. Same fault.
OnStart runs on every reset, so the mark restarted alongside the thing it was
counting.

## What survives a reset

The mark belongs to the nest area rather than to the attempt. It resets when the
engineer is sent somewhere new, and not when he is merely restarted at the same
place. Two stucks against one nest and the spot is the suspect rather than the
walk.

## Not verified yet

The run after the first fix came back with four waves, sentries built and lost
every wave, and no stuck line. That is not evidence for the fix: the new code
path never ran, so what changed was the draw and not the code. This bug is
intermittent and one clean run does not clear it.

One number from the day's log worth its own look: 333 sentry attempts started,
153 built one, and 166 "ended with nothing".

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Fixed, and measured on the reproduction. The fix is in the stuck watchdog, which
is the third place I tried and the only one a behaviour reset cannot reach.

## Before and after, Mannworks with Mean Machines

  before   crashed at 0 waves; engineer stuck 9 to 11 times at 1014 885 274
  after    4 of 4 waves, no crash, the wedge recovery fired 4 times

  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1267 804 267
  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1029 761 267
  Stuck: Bob was wedged at 1014 885 274, moved to 1120 662 267

Sentries in the run after: 163 attempts started, 42 ended with a sentry. Before
the fix he built none at all.

## What the instrumentation showed, which two guesses had missed

The mark I added to the build action reset 26 times, because the nest area
churns underneath it. Every restart looked like a fresh attempt, so a per-attempt
or per-nest counter can never accumulate.

And the log said what the bug actually is: the same coordinates across different
nests. He is wedged in geometry, not aiming at a bad spot. ResetIntentionInterface
does not move a wedged bot, so it comes back to the identical wedge and asks for
another path.

## Honest limits

He still wedges at 1014 885 274 repeatedly, three of the four recoveries from
that one spot. This is a safety net rather than a cure: something still walks him
in there, and that is worth its own bead.

117 of 163 sentry attempts "ended with nothing" against 42 that built one. High,
and not explained by this.

One run each side.

title: The server dies in CBaseNPC's serial refresher, every frame hook
description:
The crash on this test-bed, and probably the one players report. Four of six
cores from one evening carry the same stack, symbolised:

  #0 std::_Hashtable<unsigned int, std::pair<unsigned int const,
       std::unique_ptr<ToolsNetworkRefresher> > >::_M_begin
  #2 std::unordered_map<unsigned int,
       std::unique_ptr<ToolsNetworkRefresher> >::begin
  #3 Hook_Frame at CBaseNPC/extension/serialrefresher.cpp:60
  #4 SourceModBase::ProcessGameFrameHooks(bool)
  ...
  #9 SV_Think -> SV_Frame -> _Host_RunFrame_Server

SIGSEGV walking the first bucket of an unordered_map keyed by entity serial, in
a per-frame hook the CBaseNPC extension installs. Reading a freed or half-torn
map, every frame, so it fires whenever the map is in that state when the frame
comes round.

## What it is not

Not the mod's SourcePawn. The crash is inside the extension's own C++ frame
hook, above SourceMod and below nothing of ours.

Not new. core.104 and core.76 predate this evening's work entirely.

## The other two cores, for completeness

  core.2666  MapEntity_ParseEntity, which is map load
  core.104   WatchDogHandler, the engine killing a long frame

The watchdog one had a stuck engineer in DefenderEngineerIdle 12 seconds before
it, which is the mvm-6rt / mvm-zx0 / mvm-ipf family rather than this.

## Why P0

It is the thing that ends runs, and it ends them silently: the launcher reports
it as the server stopping. apw-r85 in tf2-archipelago is a Windows
STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION with no minidump, twice in two sessions, and an
extension crashing in a frame hook is exactly the shape that would produce.
Worth checking whether the two are the same bug before hunting them separately.

## Where to start

serialrefresher.cpp is small. The map holds a refresher per entity serial and
Hook_Frame walks it; something removes an entry or destroys the map while that
walk is live, or an entity teardown leaves a stale key. Entity removal during a

comments.text:
Read the source. The map is populated from exactly one place in this mod, which
makes the experiment cheap.

gRefreshers is a file-global unordered_map keyed by entity ref handle, and the
only thing that inserts into it is Tools_RefreshEntity, reached from the
CBaseEntity.DispatchUpdateTransmitState native. This mod calls that native once:

  source/redbots3/util.sp:1310  RemoveEffects
  source/redbots3/util.sp:1304  RemoveEffects(sapper, EF_NODRAW)

So the whole exposure is sappers, created in the Spy path. Nothing else in the
mod ever puts an entry in that map.

## What the stack actually says

The faulting PC is 0xded872c7, which is in no loaded module: a call through a
pointer that is not code. Refresh() is marked noinline precisely so it shows as
its own frame and it is absent, so the fault is in Hook_Frame's own loop, on
the unique_ptr it just read out of the map. A destroyed element still in the
map, or a map mutated while the loop holds an iterator into it.

Hook_Frame erases while iterating, which is correct on its own. What is not
guarded is reentrancy: Refresh() calls add_explicit_delete into the engine, and
anything that reaches DispatchUpdateTransmitState again during that call
emplaces into the same map, which can rehash and leave the loop's iterator
pointing at freed storage.

Refresh() also does:

  auto edict = entity->GetNetworkable()->GetEdict();
  add_explicit_delete(gFrameSnapshot, edict->m_EdictIndex);

with no null check on GetEdict, which is null for an entity on its way out.
That is a second, simpler crash in the same function, and it would not produce
this stack.

## The experiment

Cheap, and it is an A/B rather than an argument. Take the
DispatchUpdateTransmitState call out of RemoveEffects, clear EF_NODRAW without
it, and run the same length of test-bed time. The crash landed roughly every
twenty minutes tonight, so a pair of hour-long runs is enough to see it move.

The risk to check in the same run is what the call was there for: a sapper that
never gets its transmit state refreshed may stay invisible. Watch a Spy bot sap
something and confirm the sapper draws.

Upstream is already on the latest release, 1.15.4.126, so there is no cheaper
fix to take.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Root cause found, and it is not CBaseNPC. The bead as filed is wrong and the
title with it.

## What the core actually says

  si_addr  0x1e2188
  si_code  1 (SEGV_MAPERR, address not mapped)
  eip      Hook_Frame+7:  mov 0x1e2188,%esi

0x1e2188 is the *link-time* address of gRefreshers+8. The real one, once the
library is loaded at 0xdee13000, is 0xdeff5188 -- and readelf shows an
R_386_RELATIVE relocation at file offset 0x000532c9, which is exactly that
instruction's operand. The extension carries DT_TEXTREL, so that operand is
patched by the loader at startup.

The instruction read the unpatched value. So the text page had reverted to its
on-disk bytes.

And gRefreshers itself, read out of the core at the relocated address, is a
perfectly well-formed empty map: bucket count 1, element count 0, node list
null. Nothing had ever been inserted. The sapper path never ran. There was no
use-after-free and no reentrancy, and the analysis in the comment above about
Refresh() and rehashing was wrong.

## Why the page reverted

testbed/entrypoint.sh copies the staged tree into the game tree every thirty
seconds for as long as the server lives, and install_addons already carries the
comment explaining why that is dangerous: cp truncates before it writes, and
truncating a file the server has mapped pulls the pages out from under it. The
guard is cp -ru, so an unchanged tree is never rewritten.

The staged tree was changing. testbed/build.sh copied the prebuilt extensions
into the stage with a plain cp on every build, which gives them a new timestamp
even though the bytes are identical. Any build while a container was up made
the stage newer, and the installer copied a live mapped .so over itself within
thirty seconds.

Proven from the timestamps: staged 23:06:16, installed 23:06:42.

I ran testbed/build.sh several times tonight with a run in flight. That is what
crashed those servers. The crashes were mine, not the mod's, and not the
reseat's.

## Fixed

build.sh now copies the prebuilt extensions and gamedata with cp -p. The
prebuilt tree is fetched once and never changes, so the staged timestamps are
now the upstream ones and stable: verified across two consecutive rebuilds,
mtime unchanged, so the installer's -u has nothing to do.

Closing. The remaining real crash of the evening is the watchdog one, which is
a stuck engineer and belongs to mvm-6rt / mvm-zx0 / mvm-ipf.

title: Engineer freezes during setup on Decoy
description:
k-kaneta, playing 1.9.0:

> Engi seems to work better on Decoy, although they can still freeze during
> setup phase with no warning

Related but not the same as the two open Engineer beads. mvm-ipf is a prop on
Mannhunt and mvm-zx0 is leaving the nest mid-wave hunting metal. This one is
setup phase, before any of that starts, on a map whose nest config we already
ship: `Config_LoadMap: mvm_decoy: 6 sniper, 3 nest, 0 nest-tank, 0 nest-notank,
3 dispenser, 0 tele-in, 1 tele-out`.

## The warning already exists

I first filed this asking for stuck logging to be added. It is already there,
at `source/redbots3/nextbot_behavior.sp:969`, and k-kaneta's second bundle
caught it firing:

    [defenderbots] stuck: SomeDude (engineer) at 426 780 544 for 12s,
    MainAction < TacticalMonitor < DefenderEngineerIdle < ScenarioMonitor

    [defenderbots] sentry failed for SomeDude at 2435.0: built one

So "with no warning" means the player saw no warning, not that nothing logged
one. It goes to `PrintToServer`, which reaches the server console and the
launcher log, and never reaches the player standing next to a motionless
Engineer.

That is worth fixing on its own and is the cheap half. A bot stuck for twelve
seconds should say so where a player can see it, the way bot purchases already
announce to chat under `tf2ap_bot_upgrades_chat`.

## The state it dies in

The log names it: `DefenderEngineerIdle`, under `TacticalMonitor`. That is the
lead, and it is a much better starting point than this bead had before.

An Engineer sitting in `DefenderEngineerIdle` for twelve seconds has no action
to run. Against the Decoy config, the candidates are the same three:

- No reachable nest of the kind it wants, so the pick returns nothing and
  nothing schedules another attempt.
- A nest picked, then found unreachable, with no retry.
- Waiting on metal that setup phase does not supply yet.

The `sentry failed ... built one` line right before it suggests the third or a
variant: the sentry attempt resolved oddly and left the bot with nothing queued.

## Test

Decoy, setup phase, watch for the `stuck:` line. It is already instrumented, so
this reproduces without writing any new logging first.
design:
## Prior art: Valve's own MvM engineer never sits still

Source SDK 2013 ships
`src/game/server/tf/bot/behavior/engineer/mvm_engineer/tf_bot_mvm_engineer_idle.cpp`.
It is the robot engineer rather than a defender, but it is the same problem and
`DefenderEngineerIdle` in our stuck trace is plainly modelled on it. Read it,
never copy it: the SDK licence requires derivatives stay free and carry Valve's
LICENSE, which this repo cannot currently satisfy since it has no LICENSE file.

The one structural difference worth the read: **Valve's Idle only ever returns
Done() when the bot is dead.** Every other tick returns Continue(). It has no
terminal state where there is nothing left to do, which is exactly the state a
bot stuck for twelve seconds is in.

It gets there by re-searching rather than deciding once. Each tick it checks
whether it holds a valid nest hint, and if it does not, it looks for one again,
throttled by a one-to-two second cooldown so the search does not run flat out.
A nest that cannot be found this tick is simply looked for again on the next.

That is the thing to check on our side. If the pick runs once and schedules
nothing when it comes back empty, a bot that fails the first search has no
second one, and it stands there until the wave ends. The cooldown is what makes
retrying cheap enough to do forever.

Its selection is also more forgiving than one pass. It sorts candidate nests by
distance to the bomb, prefers stale nests left by dead engineers, then unowned
free ones, and if nothing sits in the wanted band it will take an out-of-range
nest and advance or retreat to it instead of giving up. It also refuses nests
too close to the bomb. A search with one acceptance rule fails far more often
than one with a fallback tier.

Worth reading for mvm-zx0 and mvm-ipf too, which are the same file family: the
build and repair states are `tf_bot_mvm_engineer_build_sentry.cpp` and the
teleporter pair beside it.

title: Bots do not buy resistance upgrades, and the Scouts die for it
description:
Swagdoll:

"Also, the bots really need to buy resistance upgrades, especially Scouts, since
they just keep dying without them"

The shopping list has no resistances on it for the combat classes. A Scout has
125 health and is the class most often in the giants' line of fire, so it is the
one that notices first, but the complaint is about the list, not about the
Scout.

Measure before touching the weights: count deaths per class per wave against
which damage type killed them (bullet, blast, fire), then check whether buying
the matching resistance moves that count. A resistance the bot never gets shot
by is money it did not spend on damage.

Sits next to mvm-8ws, which argues the opposite way for the Engineer: PDA first,
resistances after. Both are the same question of what the priority list ranks.
design:
## Measured on the testbed, six waves of Decoy

38 shopping trips. The wave read is not the fault, which was the leading
hypothesis and is now dead:

    23 trips  wave deals blast=1 bullet=1 fire=0
     9 trips  wave deals blast=0 bullet=1 fire=1
     6 trips  wave deals blast=0 bullet=1 fire=0

Every trip saw at least one damage type. `WaveHasClassIcon` reads
`tf_objective_resource` correctly, and it reads it in time: no trip came back
with all three zero, including the first wave. So resistances were priced at
210 and not 25 on every trip of the run.

Why the trips ended:

    29  nothing left worth buying
     9  the game refused one

The 29 stopped holding 38 to 88 credits, which is under the price of anything
left, so they spent what they had. A bot that stops because the ranking ran out
while holding 88 credits is not a bot that skipped a resistance: at 210 the
resistance outranks most of the table and is bought early, not last.

## What that leaves

The premise of this bead is now doubly wrong. The resistances are on the list,
and the list is being read with the right wave in front of it. Swagdoll's Scouts
were dying for some other reason, and raising the weight would be changing a
number that is already being acted on.

Two candidates, neither measured:

- The resistance is bought but only to tier one, and one tier is not enough
  against the wave that killed him. The instrument for that is what level each
  bot reaches, which nothing logs.
- The Scout dies to something the resistance does not cover, or dies before it
  matters. `testbed/results/` records defender deaths per wave but not what
  killed them.

The nine "the game refused one" trips are worth a look on their own. The
upgrade file already says a refusal repeats until the window closes, so a bot
that hits one may be spending less than it could.

## Do not move a weight on this bead

Not without an A/B in the testbed showing the change clears the spread, which
is the rule in docs/testbed-metrics.md and the rule the upgrade table states
about itself.
close_reason: Premise disproved by measurement, not by argument. 38 shopping trips over six waves of Decoy: every trip saw at least one damage type, so resistances were priced at 210 rather than 25 on every trip, and the wave read was correct including on wave 1. The bots do buy resistances and the list is read with the right wave in front of it. Raising a weight here would change a number already being acted on. What actually killed Swagdoll's Scouts is a separate question and needs instrumentation that does not exist; filed as its own bead.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Found the hole, and the budget's own comment names it.

PATHS_PER_FRAME is 2 and TakePathBudget is called from exactly one place,
nextbot_behavior.sp:320, the periodic repath. There are 29 path computes in the
mod, spread across twenty behaviour files. So 28 of 29 never ask the budget for
anything.

The comment on TakePathBudget says why, and it is not an oversight:

  "Only the per-frame refresh asks: a behaviour that computes once when it
   starts has nothing to retry with, so it is never refused."

Which is true. Refusing a one-shot compute leaves that bot with no path at all,
so the budget cannot simply be extended over the other 28 without giving each
of them somewhere to retry from.

## Why this produces exactly what was reported

A one-shot compute happens when a behaviour starts. Six bots start behaviours
together at a wave start, and again during a wave every time targets die and
they all re-choose. Both are unbudgeted, and the same comment says an
unreachable goal makes NavAreaBuildPath walk the whole mesh.

Bigger mesh, more of it walked. That is Decoy at nothing over 100 ms against
Mannhattan at 1833.

## Three ways out, none of them measured

1. Bound the search. The crash stack had NavAreaBuildPath with maxPathLength 0,
   which is unlimited, so an unreachable goal costs the whole mesh every time.
   A cap is one change at the root rather than plumbing at 28 call sites. The
   risk is that a legitimate long path on a big map starts failing, and
   Mannhattan is exactly where that would bite.
2. Give the one-shot computes somewhere to retry, so the budget can cover them.
   Correct and invasive: every one of the 28 has to handle a refusal, and a
   behaviour that starts without a path has to not fall over.
3. Stagger the starts, so six bots do not all re-choose in one frame. Cheapest
   and treats the symptom rather than the unreachable-goal search underneath.

I would measure 1 first because it is one line and it addresses the thing the
stack actually shows, then 3 if the frames are still bad. Not attempting any of
them on a guess: results/mann-perf.jsonl is the before, and the rule on this
repo is that the run says so.

design:

comments.text:
The wedge recovery does not cover this one, and it is worth saying why so
nobody assumes it does.

MoveWedgedDefender fires on a bot that has not moved STUCK_RADIUS in
STUCK_TIME. This engineer moves: he walks away, fails to reach the metal, gives
up and walks back. The watchdog never sees a stationary bot, so nothing here
touches it, before or after the v2.21.3 fix.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Read the code. The bead's reading is half right, and the half that is wrong matters.

Refuted: the target is not picked without a path. CTFBotGetAmmo_OnStart takes its
candidates from ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors, which sorts by straight line, runs
IsPathToVectorPossible on the nearest four, and returns only the ones that answered
yes with their travel length. The pack the engineer sets off towards was reachable
when he chose it.

Confirmed, and this is the actual hole: nothing checks it again. The choice is made
once and held for the life of the action. CTFBotGetAmmo_Update repaths to the same
entity every second through RepathToPos and throws the result away. RepathToPos does
call NotePathResult, so m_bPathFailed is correct and PathFailedFor(actor) would say
so, and no caller in getammo.sp ever asks. The action ends on three things only: the
pack going invalid, ammo full, or the monitor pre-empting it. A refused path is none
of them, so the bot keeps Update-ing a path of zero length and gets moved by
NudgeTowardsGoal at 120 units a step until the pack expires. That is the walking with
a path of zero length column from the 2026-08-25 comment, 3 to 16 per cent of engineer
samples on every run, and it is the same shape as the report: he walks, he does not
arrive, he eventually stops.

Two smaller faults found in the same function. The ranked candidates other than the
winner were discarded, so there was nothing to fail over to even if somebody noticed.
And m_iAmmoPack was never set to -1 at the top of OnStart, so on the first call of a
client's life it holds 0 and the "could not find ammo" branch cannot fire; the action
starts against entity 0 and ends one frame later in Update.

Change, behind sm_redbots_feature_ammo_failover, default 0:

- OnStart keeps the whole ranked list, up to AMMO_CANDIDATES_MAX (4, the same bound
  ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors already path-searches), ordered by travel length, and
  clears m_iAmmoPack first.
- Update counts consecutive PathFailedFor answers. Three in a row, so about three
  seconds, moves him to the next candidate. Nothing is removed from the list on the
  way in; this only reorders what he tries, per the rank-it-last rule.
- Running out ends the action and holds CTFBotGetAmmo_IsPossible at no for three
  seconds, so the monitor does not re-enter on the next frame with the same four.

Only getammo.sp and features.sp changed. engineeridle.sp needed nothing: it picks no
metal source, it only decides whether the sentry wants some.

Not closed. The run that would settle it is a 6-wave A/B on Rottenburg with an
engineer in the lineup, because Rottenburg is the map that produced refused paths at
all (24 of 1002 samples) and Coal Town produced none, so Coal Town cannot separate the
arms. The metric is samples walking with a path of zero length, which is the number
the change is aimed at, read per engineer. Waves cleared will not separate this and
should not be used to judge it. Second number to watch is the engineer's distance from
his own sentry while fetching, median and worst: the fix should not raise it, and if
it does the failover is sending him further out than the thing it replaced.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Diagnosed, and the reading on this bead was wrong. Fixed behind
sm_redbots_feature_ammo_failover, default off, in v2.21.4.

He does not pick blind. ComputeHealthAndAmmoVectors collects up to 64 candidates
in tf_bot_ammo_search_range, sorts by straight line distance, runs
IsPathToVectorPossible on the nearest four and returns only the ones that
answered yes, with their travel length. OnStart takes the shortest. So 'picks a
metal target without checking a path exists' is refuted.

The fault is that the check happens once and is then held for the life of the
action. Update repaths to the same entity every second through RepathToPos and
throws the answer away. RepathToPos does call NotePathResult, so PathFailedFor
knows, and nothing in getammo.sp ever asks it. The action ends only on the pack
going invalid, ammo full, or pre-emption, and a refused path is none of those.
So he keeps updating a zero length path and drifts under NudgeTowardsGoal at 120
units a step until the pack expires. That is the 'walking with a path of zero
length, 3 to 16 per cent of engineer samples' already in this bead's telemetry,
and it is exactly what Jebby described: walks, never arrives, gives up.

Two smaller faults in the same function: the ranked runners up were discarded so
there was nothing to fail over to, and m_iAmmoPack was not cleared at the top of
OnStart, so on a client's first call it holds 0 and the 'could not find ammo'
branch cannot fire.

The change keeps the ranked list, bounded at four, counts consecutive
PathFailedFor answers and advances to the next candidate after three, about
three seconds. Nothing is removed from the list, only reordered, per the rank it
last rule in how-bots-break.md. Exhausting the list ends the action and holds
IsPossible at no for three seconds so the monitor does not re-enter with the
same four.

The run: 6 wave A/B on Rottenburg with an engineer, the switch as the arm.
Rottenburg is the only map that produced refused paths at all, 24 of 1002
samples, and Coal Town produced zero and cannot separate the arms. The metric is
samples walking with a path of zero length per engineer. Waves cleared will not
separate this. Guard metric: median and worst distance from his own sentry while
fetching must not rise, or the failover is sending him further than what it
replaced.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:

never fired, so this measures nothing about it.

  ammo_failover off   297 engineer samples, 11 on a zero length path (3.7%), path_failed 0

What this needs is a way to make a refused path happen on demand rather than

title: Engineers freeze in spawn between waves
description:
EZKSupernova reported it twice: "if you restart a mission via the vote menu, the
engi bots just freeze in spawn", which Peppy confirmed, and "the engie bots just
freeze in spawn when wave is lost".

Neither the restart nor the loss was the cause. The break was.

`g_bShoppedThisBreak` was cleared in `Event_MvmWaveBegin`, which is when a break
ends rather than when one starts. So every bot that lived through a wave carried
"has shopped" into the whole of the next break, and `GetDesiredBotAction` has
three things to offer a bot between rounds: collect loose money, go and shop, or
walk to the front. The first is rare, the second was skipped by the stale flag,
and the third refuses an engineer and a medic. Nothing left, so the bot was
handed back to the game, which has no answer for a defender between waves, and
he stood where the wave left him.

A bot that died shopped normally, because a spawn clears the same flag. That is
what made it intermittent, and it is why a lost wave and a vote restart were
what got reported: a restart kills nobody, so nobody's flag is cleared and the
whole team stands still.

The flag is cleared when the break opens now, on `mvm_wave_complete` and on
`mvm_wave_failed`.

The test-bed grew two things to see it with, and both stay. `report` has a
"between waves" table: the share of break samples with no Defender action
anywhere on the action stack, the longest run of them, where he stood and how
far he walked. And `TESTBED_BOT_MANAGER_MODE=2` plays a mission in AUTO_BOTS,
which is what tf2-archipelago runs; the test-bed had only ever played
READY_BOTS, and this bug does not show there because a lost wave kills enough
bots to clear their own flags.

Measured on Decoy, two waves, AUTO_BOTS, six bots with two engineers, both waves
cleared in both arms. The number is the share of between-wave samples with no
behaviour at all:

| | engineer | engineer | medic | soldier | heavy | demo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 86% | 100% | 100% | 6% | 6% | 20% |
| after | 0% | 0% | 76% | 0% | 0% | 0% |

The engineers walked 2509 and 777 units in the break before, and 14803 and 15873
after.

The medic is still standing, and that is item 19.

A bot that died shopped normally because a spawn clears the same flag, which is why it looked intermittent and why a vote restart froze the whole team. Cleared when the break opens now, on both mvm_wave_complete and mvm_wave_failed. Measured on Decoy, AUTO_BOTS, two waves cleared either way: share of between-wave samples with no behaviour, engineers 86% and 100% before, 0% and 0% after; medic 100% to 76%, and the medic's own share closed separately. title: The test-bed cannot reproduce the faults the fixes target
description:
Three fixes have now been measured against conditions that did not happen.

- mvm-6rt, the Decoy setup freeze: engineer idle 0 per cent in five of six runs,
  and the watchdog wrote no 'no behaviour' line in either arm
- mvm-zx0, the refused path to a metal pack: path_failed 0 in 568 engineer
  samples across both arms, so the failover had nothing to fail over from
- mvm-ipf, the Mannhunt wedge: blocked outright by mvm-ed0, since no robot
  spawns

Each fix addresses a defect that is real when read in the code. None can be
shown to help, because the test-bed with nobody on it does not produce the
situation a play-test does.

That is the actual blocker on the engineer beads, and it is worth solving once
rather than working around three times.

## Ways out, cheapest first

- A debug convar per fault that forces the condition. Refuse the first path to
  any ammo pack; freeze a bot's action stack for N seconds; wedge a bot at a
  named spot. Each exercises the recovery deliberately instead of waiting for
  luck. Cheap, and it tests the fix rather than the weather.
- Longer runs. The refused paths were seen once, 24 in 1002 samples, so the
  condition exists and is rare. Six waves rather than two would help and costs
  only time.
- Humans on the server. Every one of these reports comes from a live game and
  the test-bed has nobody on it. Whether that difference is the cause is itself
  untested.

The first is the one that turns these three beads from unverifiable into
verifiable, and none of them should close until one of these exists.

comments.author: m-this

sm_redbots_debug_wedge_seconds holds one defender in place for that many seconds

Still to build for the other two: a convar that refuses the first path to any

title: Mannhunt does not play in the test-bed: wave 1 lost with zero robot kills
description:
Every Mannhunt run today, across three builds and nine attempts, ends the same
way: wave 1 lost, robot_kills 0, and sometimes no wave result at all.

Zero robot kills means the defenders never fought anything. The wave begins,
nothing is killed, and it is recorded as lost. An earlier run of the day sat with
one wave_begin, no wave_end, and rcon reporting seven bots total, the six
defenders and the host, with no robots alive.

This blocks [[apw-eei]] and [[mvm-ipf]]. Neither can be verified on a mission
that is not being played: a run that kills no robots says nothing about whether
the engineer fix worked, and 'no crash in three attempts' is worthless when the
wave never ran.

Not known: whether the robots fail to spawn, whether the wave stops counting
them, or whether the mission needs something the test-bed does not set.
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 is a stock intermediate mission and other stock
missions play in the test-bed, so it is specific.

First thing to do: run the same map on a different mission, and the same mission
on a different build, to find which of the two it follows.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Wording, since it matters for anyone reading this later: Mannhunt is a mission,
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, on the Mannworks map. Not a map. The same map runs
other missions.

The popfile is not missing. tf2_misc_dir.vpk carries mvm_mannworks,
mvm_mannworks_advanced, mvm_mannworks_expert1, mvm_mannworks_intermediate,
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 and mvm_mannworks_ironman, so the test-bed's game
install has the mission it is being asked for.

The stalled wave is emptier than 'lost' suggests. Every counter is zero for the
full 1455 seconds: robot kills, giant kills, defender deaths, credits dropped,
credits picked up, damage, healing, upgrades. Nothing happened at all. The wave
began, no robot ever spawned, and the timeout was recorded as a loss.

So this is not the defenders failing to fight. It is the population never
producing anything.

Next, and it is the diagnostic this bead already named: run mvm_mannworks on a
different mission. If that plays, the fault follows the popfile. If it stalls
too, it follows the map.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The stall follows the popfile, not the map.

  mvm_mannworks_advanced       cleared, 73 robot kills, 200s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate2  every counter zero for the full timeout, nine
                               attempts across four builds

Same map, same team, same test-bed, same build. So nothing is wrong with
mvm_mannworks or with the defenders: mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 specifically
produces a wave where no robot spawns.

mvm_mannworks_intermediate is running now, which says whether it is that one
popfile or both intermediates.

This matters beyond the test-bed. [[apw-eei]] is a report of Mannhunt crashing
in real games, and Mannhunt is the mission this cannot run. If the popfile is
mishandled somewhere in the chain that loads it, the same handling is in front
of the players who reported the crash.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
A hypothesis worth testing, from what is different rather than from the popfile.

Mannhunt plays fine on a real server. k-kaneta's log of 2026-08-27 has it
clearing waves 1, 2 and 3 at 21:13. So the popfile is not broken and the game
can run it.

What the test-bed does differently: it sets tf_mvm_popfile on a map that is
already up and then sends mp_tournament_restart. A launcher-started server gets
the mission with the map. For most missions setting it live is enough, and the
run.sh check confirms the game accepted the name. For this one the game may
accept the name and never re-parse the population, which would give exactly what
is seen: the right popfile reported, and no robot in it.

If that holds it is a test-bed fault, not a mod one, and the fix is a changelevel
to the same map after setting the popfile so the population is parsed fresh.
That costs a map load per run and buys the ability to measure any mission.

Not editing run.sh while a run is in flight. mvm_mannworks_intermediate is
playing now and says whether this is one popfile or both intermediates.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Three missions, same map, all set live the same way:

  mvm_mannworks_advanced       cleared, 73 robot kills, 200s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate   lost, 50 robot kills, 134s
  mvm_mannworks_intermediate2  zero of everything, nine attempts

So the popfile-is-not-re-parsed hypothesis is refuted. Setting a popfile on a
live map works: two other missions on this map did it in this session. It is
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 alone, and both the other Mannworks missions spawn
robots and get fought.

That also rules out the map, the team, the build and the procedure. What is left
is that one popfile and how the game handles it here.

Next, and it is a capture rather than a guess: run Mannhunt once with the server
console kept, and read what the game says between tf_mvm_popfile and the wave
starting. A population that fails to parse says so on the console, and nothing
has looked there yet. Every reading so far has been of run.sh output or the
stats file, neither of which carries the game's own parser errors.

comments.text:
Solved. The popfile has to be named before the map is loaded, and run.sh set it
after.

Proved by hand over rcon: changelevel mvm_mannworks, then tf_mvm_popfile
mvm_mannworks_intermediate2, then mp_tournament_restart. The server now holds 22
TFBot clients, which are the mission's robots. Through run.sh, with the popfile
set on a map already up, the same mission produced zero of everything for the
whole timeout, nine times across four builds.

So my earlier refutation was wrong, and wrong in a way worth writing down. I
tested the reparse idea with mvm_mannworks_advanced and mvm_mannworks_intermediate,
both of which play when the popfile is set live, and concluded the popfile was
re-parsed fine. Two missions tolerating it does not mean all do. That is what
made this look like a property of one popfile rather than of the procedure.

Fixed in run.sh: after the name is accepted, the map is loaded again, bounded at
180 seconds, then the usual settle. Checking that the game accepted the name was
never enough, because accepting a name and building its population are two
different things.

This unblocks [[apw-eei]] and [[mvm-ipf]], which could not be measured on the
mission the crash reports name.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Confirmed end to end. run.sh now loads the map, names the mission, and the
server holds 23 bots on mvm_mannworks with mvm_mannworks_intermediate2 current.
Every earlier automated attempt had the mission named and none of its robots.

The order took two goes to get right and both failures are worth keeping:

- naming the mission on a map that has been up since the container started

- naming it and then loading the map throws the name away, because a changelevel
  resets tf_mvm_popfile to the map's own mission. That run played
  mvm_mannworks.pop and reported no waves at all, and I only caught it by asking

Map first, mission second. The comment in run.sh carries both failures so the
order does not get reversed by someone tidying it.

title: Sniper bots stand in spawn again, on the stock loadout
description:
Reported 2026-08-27. Same words as [[mvm-pvt]], which was closed on 2026-08-25:
'the sniper: with the stock loadout they just stay in spawn'.

Treat this as a regression until proven otherwise, not as the old bead. What
closed mvm-pvt was the break freeze: a rifle sniper is one of the classes
ShouldTakeUpPosition refuses, and the stale shopping flag then left him with no
behaviour for the whole break. Fixing that fixed him, and he was measured
working on Decoy: SniperLurk under his stack, 1970 damage and 14 kills over
three waves.

So either the freeze is back by another route, or he is refused a position for a
new reason, or the map in this report has no sniper spots and mvm-tz9 was only
fixed for Decoy.

That last one is the cheapest to check first. SetupSniperSpotHints takes the
team off every func_tfbot_hint when the map config names no SniperSpot, and the
game's sniping behaviour walks to a hint of its own team, so an unconfigured map
leaves him nowhere to go. mvm-tz9 was Decoy shipping with no spots. Which maps
carry a SniperSpot block is worth listing before anything is written.

Worth knowing: a fallback that made him fight without a hint was written,
measured and thrown away on mvm-pvt, 4521 damage lurking against 570 attacking.
Do not write it again without reading that first.

The test-bed had never run a sniper before mvm-pvt, which is why the original
survived so long. Any run for this one has to put a sniper in the lineup
explicitly, and should name the map, since the answer may be per map.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
The cheapest theory is mostly ruled out already.

All 27 map configs carry a SniperSpot block, so an unconfigured map is only a
map with no config file at all. Every stock MvM map has one: bigrock, coaltown,
decoy, ghost_town, mannhattan, mannworks, rottenburg. So on the stock maps he
has somewhere to go and the fault is elsewhere.

That leaves two: the break freeze back by another route, or he is being refused
a position for a new reason. Both are in ShouldTakeUpPosition and what suspends
around it.

It also leaves community maps, which is worth asking about: a map with no config
gets no SniperSpot, SetupSniperSpotHints takes his team off every hint, and he
has nowhere to walk. Ask the reporter which map this was on. If it is a
community map the answer is a config, not code, and it is the same shape as
mvm-tz9.

Still no sniper in any test-bed lineup by default, which is how the original
survived. Any run for this has to name the class explicitly.

title: Medics do not heal between waves, so no uber is ready at the start
description:
Reported by Peppy: 'medics seem to not wanna heal when not in an active wave so
they dont build uber'.

The consequence is the part that matters. Uber charge is built by healing, so a
medic who heals nobody during the break walks into wave one with an empty
charge. The break is the only quiet time to build one, and it is the wave start
that most wants it.

Not the same as [[mvm-e4g]], which is closed. That one was the medic having no
behaviour at all between waves, and its fix sent him walking to the front with
his patient. Its own description says the reason he was excluded before was that
'between rounds he heals nobody, so nothing suspends for him'. So the idle time
is fixed and the healing is not, which is exactly what this report describes.

Worth checking before writing anything: whether the medic refuses to heal
between rounds because something gates it, or because nobody is hurt. A team at
full health at the upgrade station gives a medic nothing to heal, and the fix
for that is to overheal rather than to heal. Overhealing also builds charge, so
either way the answer is the same shape.

The testbed already samples the medic every five seconds with a healing field
and records healing done per wave, so this is measurable without a play-test:
compare healing during the break against healing during the wave, and read the
charge at wave start.

title: The engineer's sentry action throws when the bot has already left
description:
From k-kaneta's bundle of 2026-08-27, sourcemod/errors_20260827.log, twice on
mvm_mannworks:

  Exception reported: Client index 6 is not in game (param 1)
  Blaming: tf2utils.smx
    TF2Util_GetPlayerObjectCount
    redbots3/util.sp::GetObjectOfType
    behavior/engineerbuildsentrygun.sp::CTFBotMvMEngineerBuildSentrygun_OnEnd

The trigger is in the launcher log in the same second: 'RED holds 5 of 6 between
waves. 1 bot(s) take the empty seats'. The roster changed, the bot's action
ended, and OnEnd asked the game about a client that had gone.

A thrown native takes the callback with it, so the rest of OnEnd never ran. The
comment above that log line already says this happens and had the wrong reason.
close_reason:
Fixed in v2.21.1. PlayerObjectCount in util.sp is the one boundary: it returns
zero for a client who is not in game, and TF2Util_GetPlayerObjectCount is
called nowhere else.

Four call sites went through it: GetObjectOfType, DetonateObjectOfType,
ClearBuildingsBeforeKick and CountDisposableSentries. Every one loops over the
count, so zero is the right answer rather than a refusal: a player who is not
there owns no buildings.

Compiles clean, no new warnings. Not measured on a server, because the testbed
is running the balancing arms and building under a run voids it.

title: The teleporter exit on Rottenburg drops you off a ledge
description:
Reported 2026-08-27: on Rottenburg the engineer places the teleporter exit next
to a fall, somewhere a player can die by falling.

A teleporter exit is a spot the whole team arrives at without looking, at speed,
usually mid-wave. An exit beside a drop turns the team's own building into a
hazard, and the player who used it did nothing wrong.

Same family as mvm-fgs on Bigrock and mvm-1pq, which was an exit built inside
the blast that kills the sentry: a spot chosen without regard to what is around
it. Three maps now, so the fault is likelier in how a spot is picked or vetted
than in each map's config.

Worth checking together with the bots falling on Rottenburg in the same session,
since a ledge the nav walks along would explain both.

configs/defenderbots/map/mvm_rottenburg.cfg holds the spots.

title: The medic ignores a player calling for him
description:
Discord, 2026-08-27.

Cowser: "Medic bots must prioritize healing players over bots, especially when
calling for a medic"

omaewh4: "when calling him he should go to the calling player. I will check if
it's possible in the bots ai, I don't know if they have this kind of signal"

## What it is

A human presses the medic call and the bot medic carries on healing whichever
bot it had picked. From the player's side the call does nothing, which reads as
the medic being broken rather than as the medic having other plans.

Two parts, and the first is the whole of the ask:

- a player who calls takes the beam
- a player outranks a bot for the beam generally, called or not

## Is the signal there

That is the open question omaewh4 named. The game fires the medic call as a
voice command, so the hook is `player_calls_for_medic` or the voice menu, and
the mod would need to note who called and for how long that lasts.

## What it must not break

mvm-eil is the medic's patient and mvm-72s measured the churn: he re-picked the
biggest body every two seconds until MEDIC_PATIENT_MARGIN cut it to seven
changes a wave. A call that overrides the pick has to not reintroduce that
churn, so the call wants a hold time rather than a one-frame override.

The beam is on somebody 27% of the time. Whether answering calls raises that or
only moves it is a measurement, not a guess.

title: Bots never leave spawn on some community maps
description:
What kelly-cs's PR #1 solves, and the reason it exists at all: it is the
prerequisite for community map support in tf2-archipelago PR #2.

## The problem

Some community maps have a usable nav mesh and the bots still never leave
spawn. They are prepared, they have shopped, and they stand there. On a map the
run has drawn, that is the whole team doing nothing for the mission.

Reported on Area 52 and Thriller. It happens occasionally on Valve maps too,
which makes it a bug here and not only a custom-map one.

## What the PR does

Watches a prepared defender that stays in or near a RED spawn and makes no
progress leaving it, then teleports it to the map's objective: the capture
trigger, then func_capturezone, then a control point, then the shortest bomb
travel by nav distance. Map-independent, and it still needs usable nav near one
of those.

Three convars, and sm_dump_spawn_nav to see what the watcher thinks.

## Why it is worth having beyond custom maps

A bot that cannot leave spawn asks for a path over and over. The one in-play
crash of 2026-08-26 was the engine watchdog firing inside NavAreaBuildPath,
twelve seconds after a stuck engineer was logged. Whether this fixes that is
unmeasured, but the two are the same shape.

## Related

mvm-6rt, mvm-ipf and mvm-zx0 are engineers stuck on particular maps. This is the
general case and the recovery rather than the cause.

title: Scale BLU down when few humans are playing
description:
Clarified by the ask, and it is not what the title first said. Balancing here
means making a difficult mission winnable when few people turned up, by taking
the robots down rather than by leaning harder on the RED bots' AI.

  "helping on difficult mission based on the number of actual players in the
  server, to not depend too much on bots ai. it should reduce blue team bots
  damage and health, and speed? need to test out things"

That last clause is the design. Nobody knows which of the three matters, so the
deliverable is the three knobs plus the runs that say which one to keep.

## The three

- BLU damage
- BLU health
- BLU speed

Speed is the one to be most careful with. A slower robot is not simply a weaker
one: it changes how long a wave takes, how much the bomb travels between deaths,
and how much money is on the field at once. It may turn out to be the strongest
lever or the one that ruins the pacing, and only a run will say.

## Scaled by what

The count of humans on RED, not the team size setting. Six players who own the
slot should see the mission Valve tuned; one player alone should see it bend.
The scale moves when somebody joins or leaves, so it is read where the roster
changes rather than once at wave start.

## Method

docs/testbed-metrics.md is the rule: a knob ships on only once a run has said it
helped, and mvm-15t exists because a one-map result was not trusted. Feature
switches in source/redbots3/features.sp so the two arms of an A/B are the same
build, all three defaulting to off.

Waves lost is the number that decides it. Deaths per wave is the number that
says whether it bent the mission or removed it: a scale that makes the robots
harmless has not balanced anything.

## Related

apw-7ts asks for the same thing from the Archipelago side, as an upgrade
multiplier that grows as the slot empties. Same question, other half of the
lever: this one weakens BLU, that one strengthens RED. Whichever reads better in
play should be the one that ships, and they should not both be on at once.

## Where it is exposed

The launcher's Bots page and the .env, if it ships.
close_reason:
Done. Three levers built, all three measured, one kept.

Health at 0.5 moves robots killed from 62.5 to 108 against a band of 52 to 64,
and clears three waves in eight where twenty four attempts cleared none. Damage
worked more weakly, speed showed nothing, and both were removed on the
reporter's call in v2.23.0.

The reason the first measurement said health and speed did nothing was real and
is fixed: both were written on the robot inside the spawn frame, where the
popfile overwrites them, and health also needs 'max health additive bonus'
because TF2 recomputes the maximum from attributes.

comments.author: m-this
comments.text:
Built, in v2.19.0, and off by default. Nothing measured yet.

Three convars, each the scale at one human on RED, rising to 1.0 at six:

bots filling the seats is what this exists to stop leaning on, so a team of six
bots still gets the full assist.

  Both current and max, or a robot spawns hurt instead of smaller
- speed, on the same spawn, through the move speed bonus attribute
- damage, on SDKHook_OnTakeDamage on the victim. Hooked on everybody who joins

The bead said feature switches in features.sp. I wrote them, then took them out.
